text:
The child dearest to Venus went out

to his accustomed gentle conquest,

and, delayed in returning to his dwelling,

his beautiful mother took him for lost.


She goes out, runs, asks after Cupid,

impatient, anxious, frightened,

color withered, hair disheveled;

in Cyprus she sought him, in Paphos and Cnidus.


She seeks him among the nymphs she venerates

as most beautiful, in forest, river, meadow;

she seeks him among the nymphs the sea breeds.


She touched the bank of Father Tormes,

and found him here, hanging from the snowy

neck of most beautiful María.

translation.title: Lost Love
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the playful mythological search for Cupid ending at María's neck by the Tormes.
